name: Complementary Fiber Replacement Obstruction
statement: In a nontrivial old maximum sequence, if the control dimension is $m=2s+1$ with $s\ge1$, replacing even one middle fiber $B_s$ by its cube complement while keeping every other level unchanged cannot produce a maximum class.
proof: The complement has the correct cardinality and rank, but it cannot contain the nonempty lower neighbor $B_{s-1}\subseteq B_s$, and it cannot lie in the proper upper neighbor $B_{s+1}\supseteq B_s$, since then $B_s$ together with its complement would force the full control cube into $B_{s+1}$. At least one containment condition of the exact fiber criterion applies.
comments: This only obstructs a single-level equal-cardinality replacement inside the level-sum construction; it does not disprove general maximum-generated substitution.
